(a) It is obvious that we know more than animals do, and it is common to consider this one of our advantages[span_37](start_span)[span_37](end_span).

(b) You two'd better hurry up and get married.. Just do me a favour and leave me in peace[span_40](start_span)[span_40](end_span).

(c) The common people lived independently and followed their agricultural occupation[span_43](start_span)[span_43](end_span).
* Explanation: This line is derived from Mahatma Gandhi's seminal essay *Indian Civilization and Culture*[span_44](start_span)[span_44](end_span). Gandhi highlights that traditional Indian society thrived on self-reliant village communities where ordinary citizens engaged independently in farming, remaining untouched by the complex vices and eternal anxieties of urban life[span_45](start_span)[span_45](end_span).
(d) He knew nothing about the stock-market. But he knew everything about a hen[span_46](start_span)[span_46](end_span).
* Explanation: This quote is taken from H.E. Bates’ short story *The Earth*[span_47](start_span)[span_47](end_span), describing Benjy[span_48](start_span)[span_48](end_span).
